/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: An answer can't route this issue to the branch. `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` (`resolve_ref`, lines 120-153) reads `Integration branch:` / `Target branch:` only from the issue body, or from a tracking issue named there, and only when the line stands alone (regex at lines 30 and 43). Option A needs someone to edit the body. An `/answer` can't do that, and #7049 was closed (not_planned) for exactly this missing line, so picking A again would loop. Option B is the conservative fallback that still leaves room to fix something. Check-failure triage only files an issue when the base branch fails the same check (`CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_BASE_GATE_ENABLED`, default `true`), so the failure in #7049 most likely reproduces on the default branch too. Option C asks the implementer to re-run CI, which it can't do from its network-isolated sandbox, so it would end with no artefact.

Notes for the planner and implementer (from the issue spec, scoped to option B):
- Check out the default branch. Reproduce orchestrate-poll group 3, shard 0 with CI's own partition: `NR % CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_COUNT == 3` over the post-fast-fail subset, then `NR % CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS == 0`, with group count 4 and 4 shards. The partition is defined in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and checked by `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`.
- If that shard passes, run all of `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`.
- Fix only a root cause you can demonstrate, then rerun the relevant tests. Don't touch the aggregate `lint` gate in `ci.yml`.
- If nothing fails, make no code change. Record which commands ran, against which commit, and the result, and say in the PR or issue that the CI on PR #7044 (head `c659fa81b380` on `ai/issue-6769`) needs a rerun.
- A fix that lands on the default branch reaches PR #7044 when that PR next syncs with its base.

Reversibility: If an operator later puts `- Integration branch: ai/issue-6769` on its own line in the body and posts `/reclarify`, the resolver routes planning and implementation to that branch, and this answer no longer applies.
